reasoning: There are no credible state-level general-election polls or handicapping pieces specific to a 2026 North Dakota presidential or Senate race in the last 45 days, so there is no empirically grounded current 'D+ / R+' margin for those races beyond the structural lean of the state. The best available quantitative structural indicator is Cook’s Partisan Voting Index, which rates North Dakota as strongly Republican at about R+18, implying that in a neutral national environment a generic Republican would be expected to run roughly 18 points ahead of a generic Democrat statewide. Without recent, state-specific 2026 general-election polling, any more precise margin would be speculative and not supported by the required type of sources.
